nodes.label: Commit Traceability
nodes.rationale: All Git commit messages must reference the Sprint or ADR they belong to, enabling traceability from code changes back to architectural decisions.

nodes.label: Quality Assurance Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Unit test coverage must not drop below baseline (80%), and zero critical/high linting errors required before a task is considered complete.

nodes.label: Zero-Tolerance Secrets Policy
nodes.rationale: API keys, passwords, tokens, and private certificates must never be committed to the repository; environment variables or secret managers must be used instead.

nodes.label: Release and Deployment Governance
nodes.rationale: All releases follow SemVer; release notes reference closed sprints; production deployment requires staging validation sign-off.

nodes.label: Meta-Governance
nodes.rationale: Changes to governance documents (DOCUMENTATION_STYLE_GUIDE.md, WORKFLOW_RULES.md, ENGINEERING_STANDARDS.md) require an ADR and explicit Tech Lead/Architect approval.

nodes.label: Sprint Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Every standard sprint follows DESIGN -> AUDIT -> REMEDIATION -> IMPLEMENT -> AUDIT -> REMEDIATION -> VERIFY -> DONE to prevent documentation drift and state inconsistencies.

nodes.label: Documentation Is Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: docs/roadmap/, docs/implementation/, docs/architecture/, and docs/adr/ are the authoritative locations; all status reporting must reference these locations. Temporary working spaces (.gemini/, brain/, scratch/, temp/) are not sources of truth.

nodes.label: Evidence Before Status
nodes.rationale: A task may not be declared COMPLETE, PASS, APPROVED, or CLOSED without verifiable evidence such as git diff outputs, test execution logs, or coverage reports.

nodes.label: Documentation Closure Gate
nodes.rationale: Sprint closure is blocked when extra artifacts remain outside canonical files, roadmap is not updated, ADR references are inconsistent, or no designated approver has explicitly approved closure.

nodes.label: Automated Governance Checks
nodes.rationale: PRs modifying docs/ must pass automated checks: forbidden file check, sprint completeness check, and ADR naming check via pre-commit hooks or CI pipeline.

nodes.label: Workspace Lineage
nodes.rationale: Root folders are mutable and dangerous for multi-agent concurrency; workspaces are modeled as first-class, branchable domain entities with snapshot IDs to enable perfect replayability.

nodes.label: Hybrid Persistence
nodes.rationale: Event sourcing mixed with snapshotting for durable recovery; introduces complexity in recovery resolution.

nodes.label: Capability-Based Security
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for capability-based security; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Cost Governance
nodes.rationale: Risk of infinite loops addressed via pre-flight budget calculation and strict kill switches; false positives may abort valid work.

nodes.label: Execution Contracts
nodes.rationale: Enforce contracts per execution context for complex model pricing tracking; introduces overhead on prompt building.

nodes.label: Docker Sandbox Execution
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for docker sandbox execution; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Governance Layer
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for governance layer; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Coordination
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for multi-agent coordination; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Observability Platform
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for observability platform; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Architecture Freeze
nodes.rationale: Freeze Phase 1 domains (Institutional Memory, Thesis Engine, Capital Allocation Engine, Portfolio Engine) because ownership boundaries are mathematically pure, end-to-end event flow is defined, and over-optimizing without execution telemetry risks disconnection from market reality.

nodes.label: Synchronous Singleton EventBus
nodes.rationale: Implement synchronous singleton EventBus to decouple metrics aggregation; tradeoff is lack of exception isolation.

nodes.label: Artifact vs Evidence
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes between artifacts (generated outputs) and evidence (verifiable proof of execution). Scalable foundation required; monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Git Worktree Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Use git worktrees over heavy containers for MVP execution isolation; tradeoff is lower security boundary.

nodes.label: Execution Planner
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for execution planning; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: Job Queue Architecture
nodes.rationale: Scalable foundation for job queue architecture; high robustness but requires careful deployment. Monolithic/legacy approach rejected.

nodes.label: ADR-016: Capability Identity and Registration Governance
nodes.norm_label: adr-016: capability identity and registration governance

nodes.label: Capability URN Identity
nodes.rationale: All capabilities uniquely identified by structured URN: urn:karsa:capability:{namespace}:{name}:{version}. Prevents namespace collisions and enables historical reproducibility.

nodes.label: Capability Registration Governance Gate
nodes.rationale: Registering a capability is restricted to the Control Plane; capabilities transition DRAFT -> REGISTERED -> ACTIVE. Transition to ACTIVE is intercepted by GovernanceService to verify execution contracts and resource boundaries.

nodes.label: CapabilityOwner Value Object
nodes.rationale: Every capability has a designated CapabilityOwner with owner ID and type (SYSTEM, AGENT, or PARTNER), enforcing accountability.

nodes.label: ADR-017: Capability Execution Contracts and Replay Decoupling
nodes.norm_label: adr-017: capability execution contracts and replay decoupling

nodes.label: Deterministic Replay via Mock Injection
nodes.rationale: During workflow replays, the Capability Engine operates in REPLAY mode intercepting requests, bypassing the active ProviderAdapter, and fetching historical results from EvidenceRegistry. Ensures 100% deterministic, byte-for-byte identical replay.

nodes.label: ExecutionEvidence Record
nodes.rationale: Every live capability execution publishes an ExecutionEvidence record containing execution_id, correlation_id, causation_id, input/output payloads, resource metrics (CPU/memory/duration), token costs, and file artifacts.

nodes.label: CapabilityJob Serialization
nodes.rationale: The Capability Engine compiles execution requests into a serialized CapabilityJob containing target workspace snapshot_id, branch_id, and input payload, dispatched to distributed queue workers for stateless execution.

nodes.label: EvidenceRegistry
nodes.rationale: Central store for execution evidence and historical results; creates a permanent, tamper-proof audit trail. All outputs are frozen here for deterministic replay.
